patch_description: The original program failed because it returned an empty `column_orderings` list (invalid per-row orderings) and its recursive machinery mangled/misaligned DataFrames, sorted mixed-type columns (raising TypeError), and dropped the "original_index" bookkeeping inconsistently. The fix replaces the whole editable algorithm with a clean, data-preserving reordering: serialize each cell (for scoring only, never modifying stored values), build at most three bounded candidate column orderings — identity, a global frequency ordering ranked by len(v)*count(v)*(count(v)-1), and a conditional prefix-partition tree — score each candidate with the exact ideal Trie reuse metric (sum of adjacent LCP lengths of the sorted serialized rows, using C-speed slice-equality binary search instead of per-character Python loops), and return the best candidate applied as per-row column orderings. Rows and columns are never added, dropped, altered or fabricated; mixed types and NaNs are preserved by using object dtype and string conversion only in the scoring path. col_merge is honored via the parent's merging_columns as before.
